findings.message: CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY on table "orders"
findings.why: Acquires a ShareLock for the entire duration of the index build, blocking writes. On large tables this can take minutes.
findings.safePattern: Use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in its own non-transactional migration.

findings.message: Migration acquires a heavy lock but has no SET lock_timeout
findings.why: Without lock_timeout, a long-running query ahead of your DDL will block it, and then every subsequent query queues behind it (lock queue pile-up), causing an outage.
findings.safePattern: Add `SET lock_timeout = '3s';` at the top of the migration and implement application-level retry logic.

findings.message: ADD COLUMN "shipped_at" with volatile DEFAULT on table "orders"
findings.why: A volatile DEFAULT (e.g. now(), gen_random_uuid()) forces PostgreSQL to rewrite the entire table to materialise the per-row default value, holding ACCESS EXCLUSIVE for the duration.
findings.safePattern: Add the column without a DEFAULT, then SET DEFAULT, then batch-backfill existing rows outside the migration.

findings.message: ADD COLUMN "tracking_code" NOT NULL without any DEFAULT on table "orders"
findings.why: PostgreSQL must verify every existing row satisfies NOT NULL. Without a DEFAULT, the statement fails immediately on any non-empty table.
findings.safePattern: Add the column as nullable first, backfill in batches, then add NOT NULL via ADD CONSTRAINT … CHECK NOT VALID + VALIDATE CONSTRAINT.

evidence.error: column "tracking_code" of relation "orders" contains null values

findings.message: RENAME column "email" while application code still references it (3 reference(s))
findings.why: Application code references "email" in demo-repo\src\customers.ts:5, demo-repo\src\customers.ts:5, demo-repo\src\customers.ts:13. After renaming, these queries will fail.
findings.safePattern: Expand/contract: add a new column/alias, update all code to use the new name, deploy, then drop the old column in a later migration.

findings.why: A column type change forces a full table rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, blocking all reads and writes for the duration.
findings.safePattern: Add a new column with the target type, dual-write to both columns, backfill, then swap in a separate migration.

findings.message: ADD CONSTRAINT FOREIGN KEY without NOT VALID on table "order_items"
findings.why: Validating all existing rows under ShareRowExclusiveLock blocks writes to both the referencing and referenced tables for the duration of a full scan.
findings.safePattern: Use NOT VALID to skip existing row validation, then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT in a separate migration.

findings.message: Un-batched UPDATE on table "orders" without a key-range predicate
findings.why: A single-transaction UPDATE/DELETE over millions of rows holds RowExclusiveLock for the entire scan duration, accumulating a huge undo log and blocking concurrent writes.
findings.safePattern: Use a batched backfill job: `WHERE id BETWEEN :start AND :end`, processing chunks outside the schema migration.

findings.message: ALTER COLUMN "status" SET NOT NULL on table "orders"
findings.why: PostgreSQL performs a full table scan under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock to verify no NULLs remain, blocking all reads and writes.
findings.safePattern: Use: ADD CONSTRAINT … CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID; VALIDATE CONSTRAINT; then SET NOT NULL; DROP CONSTRAINT.
